# Foreign key fixtures

`fk-v2000.mdb` and `fk-v2003.mdb` are generated by
[`tools/validation/JackcessForeignKeyProbe.java`](../../tools/validation/JackcessForeignKeyProbe.java)
with the fixed Jackcess 5.2.0 JAR, and are committed so `foreign_key_v2000` /
`foreign_key_v2003` run without a JVM.

| File | Format | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `fk-v2000.mdb` | V2000 | `816695f96d4551ba643b5d98b16d8ec8459c7e777c937a4c21b14063b21323e1` |
| `fk-v2003.mdb` | V2003 | `a982cbfcd0fce07a4b0255826eeb397029dff7920a2c62a698b901286085d636` |

Each fixture holds eight relationships:

| Relationship | Tables | Referential integrity | Cascade |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ParentChild` | `Parent(Region, Code)` → `Child(ForeignRegion, ForeignCode)` | yes | updates and deletes |
| `StrictParentChild` | `StrictParent` → `StrictChild` | yes | none |
| `NullOnDelete` | `NullParent` → `NullChild` | yes | delete sets NULL |
| `ChainTopMiddle` | `ChainTop` → `ChainMiddle` | yes | updates and deletes |
| `ChainMiddleLeaf` | `ChainMiddle` → `ChainLeaf` | yes | updates and deletes |
| `TextParentChild` | `TextParent(Code)` → `TextChild(ForeignCode)` | yes | none |
| `BinParentChild` | `BinParent` → `BinChild` | yes | none |
| `GuidParentChild` | `GuidParent(Id)` → `GuidChild(ForeignId)` | yes | none |

`ParentChild` exercises the cascading path, `StrictParentChild` the plain rejection, and
`NullOnDelete` the cascade-to-NULL path. `ChainMiddle` makes its foreign key columns its primary
key, so `ChainTopMiddle` and `ChainMiddleLeaf` together force a two-level cascade. The last three
pairs cover TEXT, BINARY and GUID keys.

In every pair Jet stores the relationship alias as an extra logical index over the parent's index
data, so `Parent` and `ChainMiddle` each describe a primary key and a foreign key on one physical
index.

Regenerate after changing the generator:

```sh
javac -cp "$JACKCESS_JAR" -d "$fixture_dir" tools/validation/JackcessForeignKeyProbe.java
java -cp "$fixture_dir:$JACKCESS_JAR" JackcessForeignKeyProbe "$fixture_dir/fk-v2000.mdb" V2000
java -cp "$fixture_dir:$JACKCESS_JAR" JackcessForeignKeyProbe "$fixture_dir/fk-v2003.mdb" V2003
shasum -a 256 "$fixture_dir"/fk-v20*.mdb
```

Regeneration is only reproducible for the same Jackcess version: the fixtures follow the fixed
5.2.0 baseline commit recorded in
[`plan/Jackcess-C++重写/README.md`](../../plan/Jackcess-C++重写/README.md). Update this table and
the baseline record together when the fixture changes.

## Generated Jet4 read fixtures

Generated database files are **not committed**. The two Jet4 generators below write into the
build tree, by default `build/fixtures`, which CMake exposes as the cache variable
`REA_JACKCESS_FIXTURE_DIR` (`tests/CMakeLists.txt`). When a file is absent the matching CTest case
exits with code 77 and CTest reports it as skipped, so a clean checkout stays green.

Both generators need the fixed Jackcess 5.2.0 JAR (`$JACKCESS_JAR`) and a JDK:

```sh
javac -cp "$JACKCESS_JAR" -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rj-fixtures" tools/validation/JackcessJet4DataFixture.java
javac -cp "$JACKCESS_JAR" -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rj-fixtures" tools/validation/JackcessJet4IndexFixture.java
javac -cp "$JACKCESS_JAR" -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rj-fixtures" tools/validation/JackcessAceFixture.java
mkdir -p build/fixtures
java -cp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rj-fixtures:$JACKCESS_JAR" JackcessJet4DataFixture build/fixtures/jet4-data-v2000.mdb V2000
java -cp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rj-fixtures:$JACKCESS_JAR" JackcessJet4DataFixture build/fixtures/jet4-data-v2003.mdb V2003
java -cp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rj-fixtures:$JACKCESS_JAR" JackcessJet4IndexFixture build/fixtures/jet4-index-v2000.mdb V2000
java -cp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rj-fixtures:$JACKCESS_JAR" JackcessJet4IndexFixture build/fixtures/jet4-index-v2003.mdb V2003
java -cp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rj-fixtures:$JACKCESS_JAR" JackcessAceFixture build/fixtures/ace-v2016.accdb V2016
java -cp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rj-fixtures:$JACKCESS_JAR" JackcessAceFixture build/fixtures/ace-v2019.accdb V2019
```

Each generator prints the fixed-JAR reading of the file it just wrote, so the values can be
compared with `rea-jackcess canonical` without a comparer. Regeneration reproduces the same values
but not the same bytes: Jackcess stamps the object dates.

### Jet4 data rows

[`JackcessJet4DataFixture.java`](../../tools/validation/JackcessJet4DataFixture.java) writes
`jet4-data-v2000.mdb` and `jet4-data-v2003.mdb`. The foreign-key and query fixtures only carry
definitions, so every user table there is empty; these files add rows for the read path.

Each file holds one user table, `DataRows`, with a LONG `Id` primary key and `Flag`, `ByteVal`,
`IntVal`, `LongVal`, `FloatVal`, `DoubleVal`, `MoneyVal`, `DateVal`, `GuidVal`, `TextVal(50)`,
`BinVal(32)`, `MemoVal`, and `OleVal` columns. Six rows cover:

| Row | Coverage |
|---|---|
| 1 | every column type populated: non-ASCII text with a surrogate pair, 16-byte BINARY, 24-byte OLE, `1234.5678` MONEY, `2020-01-02 03:04:05` |
| 2 | every nullable column NULL (a NULL BOOLEAN reads back as FALSE, matching Jackcess) |
| 3 | a 9000-character MEMO that spans several data pages |
| 4 | a short MEMO updated into the cross-page value, so the row is served from an overflow row |
| 5 | boundaries: `-128`, `-32768`, `INT_MIN`, `-0.5`, `Double.MAX_VALUE`, `-0.0001`, zero GUID, empty TEXT/BINARY/MEMO/OLE, and the pre-epoch date `1899-12-29 18:30` |
| 6 | text needing JSON escaping (quote, backslash, tab, CR, LF) and CRLF inside a MEMO |

`jet4_data_read_v2000` / `jet4_data_read_v2003` assert the column definitions, all six rows,
sequential and primary key scan order, reverse scan, a primary key lookup on the migrated row, and
that the file bytes are unchanged after the read-only open.

### Jet4 composite indexes

[`JackcessJet4IndexFixture.java`](../../tools/validation/JackcessJet4IndexFixture.java) writes
`jet4-index-v2000.mdb` and `jet4-index-v2003.mdb`. The single-column fixture above cannot reach
composite TEXT keys, so these files add a second user table.

`RegionCode` holds `Id` (LONG primary key), `Region` and `Code` (TEXT 8 units), `Seq` (LONG), and
`Note` (MEMO), plus the unique ignore-nulls composite index `RegionCodeKey` over `(Region, Code)`.
The nine rows and the fixed-JAR index order are:

| Id | Region | Code | Index position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | EU | A | 4 |
| 2 | EU | B | 6 |
| 3 | US | A | 8 |
| 4 | AS | A | 2 |
| 5 | EU | C | 7 |
| 6 | NULL | Z | 1 (NULL sorts first) |
| 7 | EU | NULL | 3 (NULL code sorts before `A`) |
| 9 | US | B | 9 |
| 10 | EU | AA | 5 (`A` sorts before `AA`) |

The insertion order deliberately differs from the key order, so an index scan cannot match by
accident on physical order.

`LongValues` holds one row with a 9000-byte OLE payload that spans several data pages plus a
`BinMax` BINARY column filled to its 255-byte maximum.

`MemoKeys` carries a non-unique single-column MEMO index `MemoKeyIdx` over `(MemoKey)`. The key is
truncated to 255 UTF-16 units, so row 4 is a 606-character memo whose index entry only covers the
prefix, while the row itself must still read all 606 characters. NULL sorts first:

| Id | MemoKey | Index position | BinMax |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | memo-b | 3 | 255 bytes |
| 2 | memo-a | 2 | 255 bytes |
| 3 | memo-c | 4 | 255 bytes |
| 4 | `memo-d` + 600 `x` | 5 (truncated key) | 255 bytes |
| 5 | NULL | 1 (NULL sorts first) | empty |

`MixedKeys` adds a unique composite index over `(Tag, MemoKey)`, so the second key column is a
MEMO truncated to 255 UTF-16 units. Row 4 stores a 406-character memo: the index entry keeps the
prefix, the row keeps the full text, and a NULL tag sorts first.

| Id | Tag | MemoKey | Index position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | EU | memo-b | 3 |
| 2 | EU | memo-a | 2 |
| 3 | US | memo-a | 5 |
| 4 | EU | `memo-c` + 400 `y` | 4 (truncated key) |
| 5 | NULL | memo-z | 1 (NULL sorts first) |

The generator also attempts to insert a duplicate `(EU, memo-b)` and requires the fixed JAR to
reject it, which documents why the generated file never contains a unique-key conflict.

`jet4_index_read_v2000` / `jet4_index_read_v2003` compare the composite index order, the reverse
order, an `EU` prefix scan (both directions), the `[EU/A, US/A)` range, an exact composite lookup,
the MEMO index order in both directions, the truncated-key row text, the 255-byte BINARY payload,
the full OLE payload, the `(Tag, MemoKey)` composite index order and its prefix scan, and assert the
file bytes stay unchanged.

Jackcess stores a NULL key part as an index entry rather than skipping it, and it rejects a second
fully-NULL key as a duplicate of the first, so the fixture keeps only one NULL per key position.

### ACE V2016 and extra V2019

[`JackcessAceFixture.java`](../../tools/validation/JackcessAceFixture.java) writes
`ace-v2016.accdb` and `ace-v2019.accdb`. The committed ACE fixtures stop at V2010 plus the
single-table V2019 extended-date resource, so V2016 had no sample at all.

`V2016Data` holds `Id`, `Flag`, `Name` (TEXT 30 units), `Amount` (MONEY), `Created`
(SHORT_DATE_TIME), `Ref` (GUID), `Memo`, and `Payload` (OLE) with three rows: a fully populated row
whose MEMO passes 5000 characters, an all-NULL row, and a row with empty TEXT, MEMO, and OLE
payloads. `V2019Data` holds `Id`, `Stamp` (EXT_DATE_TIME), and `Note` with six rows: NULL,
`2020-01-02 03:04:05.123456789` (stored as 100 ns ticks, so it reads back as `123456700`), the years
100, 1265, and 1765, and the pre-epoch `1899-12-29 18:30`.

`ace_extra_read_v2016` / `ace_extra_read_v2019` assert the schema, every row value, and that the
file bytes are unchanged after the read-only open. Both also read the system table `MSysResources`
and require its `Data` column to expose the stored complex-value foreign key as a LONG, which is
what Jackcess returns for that column.

## Real sample comparison tools

`test_data_only_read/test_mdb.mdb` is a real 1.5 MB Jet4 PGeo database with 43 user tables (Chinese
names, spatial `SHAPE` BLOBs, `GDB_*` catalog tables) and 4 system tables. It stays outside version
control; `real_sample` only registers when a local copy exists and pins its SHA-256
`0bc0acb9c732de1e17c43c2d0a6019f7b5a62ccf83c5818a1bc42db7dbc460c6`.

The full schema and row comparison against the fixed Jackcess 5.2.0 JAR uses two committed tools:

```sh
# C++ side
build/rea-jackcess canonical test_data_only_read/test_mdb.mdb > /tmp/cpp.json

# Fixed JAR side
javac -cp "$JACKCESS_JAR" -d /tmp tools/validation/JackcessTableDump.java
java -cp "/tmp:$JACKCESS_JAR" JackcessTableDump test_data_only_read/test_mdb.mdb /tmp/java.json

python3 -I tools/validation/compare_table_dump.py /tmp/cpp.json /tmp/java.json
```

The comparer treats tables as row multisets and normalises formatting-only differences: decimals
compare numerically, dates by calendar fields, GUIDs without braces or case, BLOBs by length and
SHA-256, floats with a small relative tolerance. It exits 0 only when every table, column, and
value matches. On 2026-11-26 the run reported `Compared 47 tables: schema and rows match.`

## ACE complex-column read fixtures

`complex-data-v2007.accdb`, `complex-data-v2010.accdb` and `unsupported-fields-v2007.accdb` are the
Jackcess 5.2.0 test resources `complexDataV2007.accdb`, `complexDataV2010.accdb` and
`unsupportedFieldsV2007.accdb` from the fixed upstream commit. They are Apache License 2.0 test data
and are committed unchanged so the ACE schema/row tests run without a JVM.

| File | Format | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `complex-data-v2007.accdb` | V2007 | `66c655ad9f9f290c51ed808d704c2a09a7b0d6047583c6a4c67405f708cac0c3` |
| `complex-data-v2010.accdb` | V2010 | `c9707ec54fd4f712c74ee3638963ad203fc60340f5bb7ad0c86bc2878a91e6df` |
| `unsupported-fields-v2007.accdb` | V2007 | `26f3cb28640ddc018d9093cbdf3343dac612fefc656182bf6592b00ad60ac705` |

The tests check public format/schema enumeration,
`MSysComplexColumns` links to the type/flat tables, attachment/multi-value/version-history classification,
the flat-table AutoNumber primary keys and flagged foreign-key columns, ordinary row traversal and explicit rejection of ACE read-write
opens. `ace2007_unsupported_complex` also checks that the upstream `UnknownComplex` column is classified as unsupported
while its three ordinary table rows remain readable. The tests compare multi-value and version-history text/order, attachment metadata and decoded file data, unsupported-value counts and encoded unknown-field bytes, and ACE write rejection. A separate wrapper test covers raw payload decoding and malformed headers. The upstream source and broader complex-value expectations are recorded in the
[`baseline record`](../../plan/Jackcess-C++重写/04-P0基线核验记录.md#2026-11-20-ace-复杂列样本与键关系).

## ACE V2019 extended-date read fixture

`ext-date-v2019.accdb` is the unchanged Jackcess 5.2.0 test resource `V2019/extDateV2019.accdb` (Apache License 2.0, 557,056 bytes, SHA-256 `bb6d7af8e5275c1143b5f68447b2f96bd11e460fbec6856de7b3e339ccb53cf6`). `ace2019_read` checks ACE V2019 recognition and reads `Table1.ID`, `DateExt`, and the stored result in calculated column `DateNormalCalc`. The fixed-JAR checker validates all nine rows, including NULL, nanosecond precision, and years 100, 1265, and 1765; calculated expressions are not evaluated. Newer system-table behavior remains outside this check. See [`JackcessExtendedDateCheck.java`](../../tools/validation/JackcessExtendedDateCheck.java).

## ACE V2010 calculated-field read fixture

`calc-fields-v2010.accdb` is the unchanged Jackcess 5.2.0 test resource `V2010/calcFieldV2010.accdb` (Apache License 2.0, 712,704 bytes, SHA-256 `bf95642c1e661b7fb7f615124bbb8dcc614c539fff080947ae24a1e3d6ea07dd`). The `ace2010_calculated_fields` test checks `ResultType` logical typing and the four stored rows for Boolean, TEXT, MEMO, LONG, MONEY, FLOAT, and NUMERIC results. Both C++ and the fixed-JAR checker read stored results only; neither evaluates calculated expressions. See [`JackcessCalculatedFieldCheck.java`](../../tools/validation/JackcessCalculatedFieldCheck.java) and the upstream [`CalcFieldTest.readCalcFields`](../../../jackcess/src/test/java/io/github/spannm/jackcess/impl/CalcFieldTest.java).

## Saved query fixtures

`query-v2000.mdb` and `query-v2003.mdb` are the saved-query databases shipped with the Jackcess
5.2.0 test resources (`queryTestV2000.mdb` and `queryV2003.mdb` upstream, Apache License 2.0). They
are committed unchanged so `saved_query_v2000` / `saved_query_v2003` can compare
`QueryInfo::to_sql()` against the SQL the fixed JAR prints for the same file.

| File | Format | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| `query-v2000.mdb` | V2000 | `03b303034e1d64779d9dff1e19d9e21d59d8fa440dc5da9dbcfd85ad051eb5ea` |
| `query-v2003.mdb` | V2003 | `ff3512007fcbe9bf8019ec386fa4382396947b7ef3c06dfb3aa0c63f48ab88ba` |

Each file holds nine saved queries: SELECT, UPDATE, APPEND, DELETE, MAKE TABLE, CROSSTAB, UNION,
passthrough and data definition. Their expected SQL lives in `tests/query_test.cpp`; keep it in
sync with the fixtures, and re-verify with the fixed JAR before changing either.

## Descending foreign key index

Neither Jackcess nor Access creates a descending index for a relationship, so this fixture does
not carry one. The writer accepts a descending key on the child index, which was checked once on
a copy whose ascending flag was cleared by hand and reopened with the fixed Jackcess 5.2.0; see
[the baseline record](../../plan/Jackcess-C++重写/04-P0基线核验记录.md). Keep that in mind before
relying on such files: only hand-edited databases are known to contain them.

## Whole-file cross-check against the fixed JAR

`tools/validation/compare_all_samples.sh` dumps every table from both sides and compares them:

```sh
JACKCESS_CLASSPATH="/path/to/jackcess-5.2.0.jar:/path/to/commons-lang3-3.14.0.jar:/path/to/commons-logging-1.2.jar" \
    tools/validation/compare_all_samples.sh ./build/rea-jackcess \
    tests/fixtures/*.mdb tests/fixtures/*.accdb build/fixtures/*.mdb build/fixtures/*.accdb
```

The C++ side is `rea-jackcess canonical`; the Java side is `JackcessTableDump`, which writes a JSON
dump of the same shape. `compare_table_dump.py` then compares table names, column names, column
types, column lengths and rows as multisets, with these deliberate normalisations:

- a calculated column is compared by the type it exposes (`effectiveType`), not the stored type,
- a complex-value column compares the foreign-key number, which Jackcess prints as text,
- a `FLOAT` (4-byte) column compares at float32 accuracy, because the text forms differ in the last
  digits,
- an unsupported ("unknown") column keeps the row payload as length plus SHA-256, and Jackcess's
  `RawData[(n) XX ..]` text is decoded back to the same bytes before hashing,
- `f_<guid>_<column>` flat tables appear only in the C++ dump; the Jackcess dump skips them on
  purpose, so they are not reported as a difference.

A column whose MDB type has no canonical name prints as `note:` rather than failing; the type name
then follows Jackcess and becomes `UNSUPPORTED_FIXEDLEN` or `UNSUPPORTED_VARLEN` by length class.
The canonical JSON keeps `mdbType` (stored type) and adds `calculated`, plus `effectiveType` and
`effectiveCanonicalType` when a calculated column's ResultType differs.
